Assess the codebase and study how the ChromeDevTools protocol integration is handled and compare against the official specification. Also do the following:

- Identify any loopholes and impracticalities in the current implementation
- Figure out the unusable/redundant features currently implemented or suggest more useful ones when we're debugging sketches
- Verify that the keybindings used to access the features are intuitive and respect Neovim defaults
- Suggest working fixes and make the code more robust and have graceful fallback


Feel free to argue and have an opinion on the matter. Don't be a 'yes man'
I'll start by exploring the codebase structure to understand what we're working with.

664: C._start_sse_job = function()
665: 	if C.state.job_id then
666: 		return
667: 	end
668: 	if not check_curl() then
669: 		return
670: 	end
671: 	local url = string.format("http://localhost:%d/api/cdp/stream", C.state.port)
672: 	C.state.job_id = vim.fn.jobstart({ "curl", "-s", "-N", "--max-time", "3600", url }, {
673: 		on_stdout = function(_, data)
674: 			if not data then
675: 				return
676: 			end
677: 			local buf = C.state.sse_buffer or ""
678: 			for _, chunk in ipairs(data) do
679: 				buf = buf .. (chunk or "")
680: 			end
681: 			local lines = vim.split(buf, "\n", { plain = true })
682: 			C.state.sse_buffer = table.remove(lines) or ""
683: 			for _, line in ipairs(lines) do
684: 				if line ~= "" then
685: 					local ok, ev = pcall(vim.json.decode, line)
686: 					if ok then
687: 						vim.schedule(function()
688: 							C._on_event(ev)
689: 						end)
690: 					end
691: 				end
692: 			end
693: 		end,
694: 		on_exit = function()
695: 			vim.schedule(function()
696: 				C.state.job_id = nil
697: 				C.state.sse_buffer = ""
698: 				if C.state.buf and is_buf(C.state.buf) and C.state.connected then
699: 					notify("CDP stream disconnected, reconnecting...", "info")
700: 					vim.defer_fn(function()
701: 						C._start_sse_job()
702: 					end, 1000)
703: 				end
704: 			end)
705: 		end,
706: 	})
707: end

709: C._on_event = function(data)
710: 	local t = data.type
711: 	if t == "console" then
712: 		local cd = C.tab_data.console
713: 		table.insert(cd, data)
714: 		if #cd > 1000 then
715: 			table.remove(cd, 1)
716: 		end
717: 		if C.state.active_tab == 1 then
718: 			C.render_all()
719: 		end
720: 	elseif t == "network" then
721: 		local nd = C.tab_data.network
722: 		table.insert(nd, data)
723: 		if #nd > 500 then
724: 			table.remove(nd, 1)
725: 		end
726: 		if C.state.active_tab == 2 then
727: 			C.render_all()
728: 		end
729: 	elseif t == "debugger" then
730: 		C.tab_data.debugger = data
731: 		if data.event == "paused" then
732: 			local frames = data.callFrames or {}
733: 			if #frames > 0 then
734: 				C._highlight_paused(frames[1].url, frames[1].line)
735: 			end
736: 		elseif data.event == "resumed" then
737: 			C._clear_debug_highlights()
738: 		end
739: 		if C.state.active_tab == 4 then
740: 			C.render_all()
741: 		end
742: 	elseif t == "perf" then
743: 		local pd = C.tab_data.perf
744: 		if data.fps then
745: 			table.insert(pd.fps, data.fps)
746: 			if #pd.fps > 100 then
747: 				table.remove(pd.fps, 1)
748: 			end
749: 		end
750: 		if data.heap then
751: 			pd.heap = data.heap
752: 		end
753: 		if data.nodes then
754: 			pd.nodes = data.nodes
755: 		end
756: 		if data.listeners then
757: 			pd.listeners = data.listeners
758: 		end
759: 		if C.state.active_tab == 5 then
760: 			C.render_all()
761: 		end
762: 	elseif t == "status" then
763: 		local was_connected = C.state.connected
764: 		C.state.connected = (data.state == "connected")
765: 		C.state.page_url = data.url or ""
766: 		if was_connected and not C.state.connected and C.state.buf and is_buf(C.state.buf) then
767: 			if C.state.mode == "panel" then
768: 				notify("CDP disconnected, reconnecting...", "info")
769: 				vim.defer_fn(function()
770: 					if C.state.buf and is_buf(C.state.buf) then
771: 						C.connect()
772: 					end
773: 				end, 1000)
774: 			end
775: 		end
776: 		if C.state.buf and is_buf(C.state.buf) then
777: 			C.render_all()
778: 		end
779: 	end
780: end

782: C._highlight_paused = function(url, line)

789: 	local abs_path = project_root .. url_path:gsub("/$", "")
790: 	for _, buf in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_bufs()) do

816: C._fetch_lsp_symbols = function()
817: 	C.tab_data.info.symbols = {}
818: 	local bufnr
819: 	for _, b in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_bufs()) do
820: 		if vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(b):match("sketch%.js$") then
821: 			bufnr = b
822: 			break
823: 		end
824: 	end
825: 	bufnr = bufnr or vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
826: 	if not bufnr then
827: 		return
828: 	end
829: 	local clients = vim.lsp.get_clients({ bufnr = bufnr })
830: 	if #clients == 0 then
831: 		return
832: 	end
833: 	local ok, result = pcall(vim.lsp.buf_request_sync, bufnr, "textDocument/documentSymbol", {
834: 		textDocument = { uri = vim.uri_from_bufnr(bufnr) },
835: 	}, 1000)
836: 	if not ok or not result then
837: 		return
838: 	end
839: 	for _, res in ipairs(result) do
840: 		if res.result then
841: 			local function flatten(symbols, depth)
842: 				depth = depth or 0
843: 				for _, sym in ipairs(symbols) do
844: 					local kind_name = ({
845: 						"File",
846: 						"Module",
847: 						"Namespace",
848: 						"Package",
849: 						"Class",
850: 						"Method",
851: 						"Property",
852: 						"Field",
853: 						"Constructor",
854: 						"Enum",
855: 						"Interface",
856: 						"Function",
857: 						"Variable",
858: 						"Constant",
859: 						"String",
860: 						"Number",
861: 						"Boolean",
862: 						"Array",
863: 						"Object",
864: 						"Key",
865: 						"Null",
866: 						"EnumMember",
867: 						"Struct",
868: 						"Event",
869: 						"Operator",
870: 						"TypeParameter",
871: 					})[sym.kind] or "Unknown"
872: 					local icon = ({
873: 						Method = "ƒ",
874: 						Function = "ƒ",
875: 						Variable = "◆",
876: 						Constant = "◇",
877: 						Class = "○",
878: 						Property = "●",
879: 						Field = "●",
880: 					})[kind_name] or "·"
881: 					table.insert(C.tab_data.info.symbols, {
882: 						name = sym.name,
883: 						kind = kind_name,
884: 						icon = icon,
885: 						depth = depth,
886: 						lnum = (sym.range or {}).start and sym.range.start.line + 1 or 0,
887: 					})
888: 					if sym.children then
889: 						flatten(sym.children, depth + 1)
890: 					end
891: 				end
892: 			end
893: 			if type(res.result) == "table" then
894: 				flatten(res.result)
895: 			end
896: 		end
897: 	end
898: end

922: C._render_tab_bar = function()

926: 	for i, tab in ipairs(tabs) do
927: 		if i > 1 then
928: 			table.insert(parts, "│")
929: 		end
930: 		local label = string.format("%s:%s", tab.key, tab.name)
931: 		if counts[i] > 0 then

933: 		end
934: 		if i == C.state.active_tab then
935: 			label = "▎" .. label
936: 		else
937: 			label = " " .. label

941: 	table.insert(parts, "  [X]")
942: 	local dot

945: 	else

947: 	end

952: C._apply_highlights = function()
953: 	local buf = C.state.buf
954: 	if not buf or not is_buf(buf) then
955: 		return
956: 	end
957: 	vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, -1, 0, -1)
958: 	local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, -1, false)
959: 	local tab_line = lines[1] or ""
960: 	for _, tab in ipairs(tabs) do
961: 		local pattern = string.format("▎%d:%s", tab.key, tab.name)
962: 		local start_idx = tab_line:find(pattern, 1, true)
963: 		if start_idx then
964: 			vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, "P5CDPActiveTab", 0, start_idx - 1, start_idx - 1 + #pattern)
965: 		else
966: 			local raw = string.format(" %d:%s", tab.key, tab.name)
967: 			local raw_start = tab_line:find(raw, 1, true)
968: 			if raw_start then
969: 				vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, "P5CDPTab", 0, raw_start - 1, raw_start - 1 + #raw)
970: 			end
971: 		end
972: 	end
973: 	local close_start = tab_line:find("[X]", 1, true)
974: 	if close_start then
975: 		vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, "P5CDPClose", 0, close_start - 1, close_start + 2)
976: 	end
977: 	local connected_dot = tab_line:find("●", 1, true)
978: 	if connected_dot then
979: 		local hl = C.state.connected and "P5CDPConnected" or "P5CDPDisconnected"
980: 		vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, hl, 0, connected_dot - 1, connected_dot)
981: 	end
982: 	local k = C.state.active_tab
983: 	for ln = 3, #lines do
984: 		local l = lines[ln] or ""
985: 		if k == 1 then
986: 			local level = l:match("%[%d+:%d+:%d+%]%s+(%w+)")
987: 			if level == "ERROR" then

337:     async def _message_loop(self):
338:         assert self.ws is not None
339:         try:
340:             async for message in self.ws:
341:                 try:
342:                     data = json.loads(message)
343:                     await self._handle_message(data)
344:                 except json.JSONDecodeError:
345:                     continue
346:         except websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed:
347:             self.connected = False
348:             self._emit('status', {'state': 'disconnected'})

352:     async def _handle_message(self, data: dict):
353:         if 'id' in data:
354:             future = self._pending.pop(data['id'], None)
355:             if future and not future.done():
356:                 if 'error' in data:
357:                     future.set_exception(
358:                         Exception(data['error'].get('message', 'CDP error'))
359:                     )
360:                 else:
361:                     future.set_result(data.get('result', {}))
362:             return
363:         method = data.get('method', '')
364:         params = data.get('params', {})
365:         if method == 'Runtime.consoleAPICalled':
366:             await self._handle_console_api(params)
367:         elif method == 'Runtime.exceptionThrown':
368:             await self._handle_exception(params)
369:         elif method == 'Network.requestWillBeSent':
370:             self._handle_request_sent(params)
371:         elif method == 'Network.responseReceived':
372:             self._handle_response(params)
373:         elif method == 'Network.loadingFailed':
374:             self._handle_load_failed(params)
375:         elif method == 'Debugger.scriptParsed':
376:             self._scripts[params.get('url', '')] = params.get('scriptId', '')
377:         elif method == 'Debugger.paused':
378:             await self._handle_paused(params)
379:         elif method == 'Debugger.resumed':
380:             self._emit('debugger', {'event': 'resumed'})
381:         elif method == 'Performance.metrics':
382:             self._handle_perf(params)
383:         elif method == 'Timeline.eventRecorded':
384:             pass

386:     async def _handle_console_api(self, params: dict):
387:         level_map = {
388:             'warning': 'warn', 'error': 'error',
389:             'debug': 'log', 'info': 'info', 'log': 'log',
390:         }
391:         level = level_map.get(params.get('level', 'log'), 'log')
392:         args = params.get('args', [])
393:         messages = []
394:         for a in args:
395:             t = a.get('type', '')
396:             if t == 'string':
397:                 messages.append(a.get('value', ''))
398:             elif t == 'object':
399:                 messages.append(a.get('description', ''))
400:             elif t == 'number' or t == 'boolean':
401:                 messages.append(str(a.get('value', '')))
402:             else:
403:                 messages.append(a.get('description', str(a.get('value', ''))))
404:         message = ' '.join(messages)
405:         stack = []
406:         if 'stackTrace' in params:
407:             for f in params['stackTrace'].get('callFrames', []):
408:                 stack.append({
409:                     'function': f.get('functionName', '<anon>'),
410:                     'url': f.get('url', ''),
411:                     'line': f.get('lineNumber', 0) + 1,
412:                     'column': f.get('columnNumber', 0) + 1,
413:                 })
414:         self._emit('console', {
415:             'level': level, 'message': message,
416:             'timestamp': datetime.now().strftime('%H:%M:%S'),
417:             'stack': stack,
418:         })

420:     async def _handle_exception(self, params: dict):
421:         ed = params.get('exceptionDetails', {})
422:         exc = ed.get('exception', {})
423:         msg = exc.get('description', exc.get('value', 'Unknown error'))
424:         stack = []
425:         for f in ed.get('stackTrace', {}).get('callFrames', []):
426:             stack.append({
427:                 'function': f.get('functionName', '<anon>'),
428:                 'url': f.get('url', ''),
429:                 'line': f.get('lineNumber', 0) + 1,
430:                 'column': f.get('columnNumber', 0) + 1,
431:             })
432:         self._emit('console', {
433:             'level': 'error', 'message': msg,
434:             'timestamp': datetime.now().strftime('%H:%M:%S'),
435:             'stack': stack,
436:         })

438:     def _handle_request_sent(self, params: dict):
439:         req_id = params.get('requestId', '')
440:         req = params.get('request', {})
441:         self.pending_requests[req_id] = {
442:             'method': req.get('method', 'GET'),
443:             'url': req.get('url', ''),
444:             'start_time': datetime.now().timestamp(),
445:             'status': None, 'status_text': None,
446:             'size': None, 'error': None,
447:         }

449:     def _handle_response(self, params: dict):
450:         req_id = params.get('requestId', '')
451:         resp = params.get('response', {})
452:         p = self.pending_requests.pop(req_id, None)
453:         if not p:
454:             return
455:         p['status'] = resp.get('status', 0)
456:         p['status_text'] = resp.get('statusText', '')
457:         p['size'] = resp.get('transferSize', 0)
458:         p['end_time'] = datetime.now().timestamp()
459:         p['duration_ms'] = round((p['end_time'] - p['start_time']) * 1000, 1)
460:         self.completed_requests.append(dict(p))
461:         self._emit('network', {
462:             'method': p['method'], 'url': p['url'],
463:             'status': p['status'], 'duration': p['duration_ms'],
464:             'size': p['size'],
465:         })
466: 
467:     def _handle_load_failed(self, params: dict):
468:         req_id = params.get('requestId', '')
469:         p = self.pending_requests.pop(req_id, None)
470:         if not p:
471:             return
472:         p['status'] = 0
473:         p['error'] = params.get('errorText', 'Failed')
474:         p['end_time'] = datetime.now().timestamp()
475:         p['duration_ms'] = round((p['end_time'] - p['start_time']) * 1000, 1)
476:         self.completed_requests.append(dict(p))
477:         self._emit('network', {
478:             'method': p['method'], 'url': p['url'],
479:             'status': 0, 'error': p['error'],
480:             'duration': p['duration_ms'],
481:         })
482: 
483:     def _handle_perf(self, params: dict):
484:         metrics = params.get('metrics', [])
485:         data = {'fps': 60, 'heap': 0, 'nodes': 0, 'listeners': 0}
486:         for m in metrics:
487:             name = m.get('name', '')
488:             value = m.get('value', 0)
489:             if name == 'JSHeapUsedSize':
490:                 data['heap'] = int(value)
491:             elif name == 'JSHeapTotalSize':
492:                 data['heap'] = max(data.get('heap', 0), int(value))
493:             elif name == 'DOMNodes':
494:                 data['nodes'] = int(value)
495:             elif name == 'EventListeners':
496:                 data['listeners'] = int(value)
497:             elif name == 'FPS':
498:                 data['fps'] = int(round(value))
499:         self._perf_metrics.append(data)
500:         self._emit('perf', data)
501: 
502:     async def _handle_paused(self, params: dict):
503:         frames = []
504:         for f in params.get('callFrames', []):
505:             loc = f.get('location', {})
506:             frames.append({
507:                 'function': f.get('functionName', '<anon>'),
508:                 'url': f.get('url', ''),
509:                 'line': loc.get('lineNumber', 0) + 1,
510:                 'column': loc.get('columnNumber', 0) + 1,
511:             })
512:         self._emit('debugger', {
513:             'event': 'paused',
514:             'reason': params.get('reason', 'other'),
515:             'callFrames': frames,

519: class LiveReloadServer:
520:     """WebSocket server for live reload using asyncio."""
521:     
522:     def __init__(self, port: int, directory: str, file_watcher):
523:         self.port = port
524:         self.directory = directory
525:         self.file_watcher = file_watcher
526:         self.clients = set()
527:         self.server = None
528:     
529:     async def handler(self, websocket):
530:         """Handle WebSocket client connection."""
531:         self.clients.add(websocket)
532:         try:
533:             await websocket.send(json.dumps({"type": "connected", "message": "Live reload connected"}))
534:             await websocket.wait_closed()
535:         except (websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK, websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError):
536:             pass
537:         finally:
538:             self.clients.discard(websocket)
539:     
540:     async def start(self):
541:         """Start the WebSocket server."""
542:         for offset in range(10):
543:             try:
544:                 self.server = await websockets.serve(
545:                     self.handler, 'localhost', self.port + offset
546:                 )
547:                 if self.server.sockets:
548:                     self.port = self.server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
549:                 print(f"Live reload WebSocket running on ws://localhost:{self.port}")
550:                 return
551:             except OSError:
552:                 continue
553:         print("Warning: Could not start live reload server")
554:     
555:     async def broadcast(self, message: dict):
556:         """Broadcast message to all connected clients."""
557:         data = json.dumps(message)
558:         
559:         # Take a snapshot to avoid concurrent modification during iteration
560:         clients_snapshot = set(self.clients)
561:         disconnected = set()
562:         
563:         for client in clients_snapshot:
564:             try:
565:                 await client.send(data)
566:             except (websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK, websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError, websockets.exceptions.InvalidState):
567:                 disconnected.add(client)
568:             except Exception:
569:                 disconnected.add(client)
570:         
571:         for client in disconnected:
572:             self.clients.discard(client)
573:             try:
574:                 await client.close()
575:             except Exception:
576:                 pass
577:     
578:     async def close(self):
579:         """Close the server and all connections."""
580:         for client in list(self.clients):
581:             try:
582:                 await client.close()
583:             except Exception:
584:                 pass
585:         self.clients.clear()
586:         if self.server:
587:             self.server.close()
588:             await self.server.wait_closed()

591: class FileWatcher:
592:     """Async file watcher using asyncio."""
593:     
594:     def __init__(self, directory: str, extensions: list, exclude_dirs: list, debounce_ms: int):
595:         self.directory = directory
596:         self.extensions = extensions
597:         self.exclude_dirs = exclude_dirs
598:         self.debounce_ms = debounce_ms / 1000
599:         self.last_trigger = 0
600:         self.running = False
601:         self._task: Optional[asyncio.Task] = None
602:     
603:     def should_watch(self, path: str) -> bool:
604:         """Check if file should be watched."""
605:         path_obj = Path(path)
606:         
607:         # Check exclusion dirs
608:         for part in path_obj.parts:
609:             if part in self.exclude_dirs:
610:                 return False
611:         
612:         # Check extensions
613:         return any(str(path).endswith(ext) for ext in self.extensions)
614:     
615:     async def watch(self):
616:         """Watch for file changes - only trigger on actual file saves."""
617:         self.running = True
618:         last_mtimes = {}
619:         pending_changes = {}  # Track files that have changed but not yet stable
620:         
621:         while self.running:
622:             try:
623:                 current_mtimes = {}
624:                 for root, dirs, files in os.walk(self.directory):
625:                     dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in self.exclude_dirs]
626:                     
627:                     for file in files:
628:                         path = os.path.join(root, file)
629:                         if self.should_watch(path):
630:                             try:
631:                                 current_mtimes[path] = os.path.getmtime(path)
632:                             except OSError:
633:                                 continue
634:                 
635:                 now = datetime.now().timestamp()
636:                 
637:                 # Check for actual file changes (mtime differs from last known)
638:                 for path, mtime in current_mtimes.items():
639:                     last_mtime = last_mtimes.get(path)
640:                     
641:                     if last_mtime is None:
642:                         # First time seeing this file - skip
643:                         continue
644:                     
645:                     if mtime != last_mtime:
646:                         # File has changed - mark as pending
647:                         if path not in pending_changes:
648:                             pending_changes[path] = now
649:                 
650:                 # Check pending changes for stability
651:                 for path, change_time in list(pending_changes.items()):
652:                     current_mtime = current_mtimes.get(path)
653:                     last_mtime = last_mtimes.get(path)
654:                     
655:                     if current_mtime is None:
656:                         # File was deleted
657:                         del pending_changes[path]
658:                         continue
659:                     
660:                     if current_mtime == last_mtime and (now - change_time) >= self.debounce_ms:
661:                         # File is stable (not changing) and has been stable long enough
662:                         del pending_changes[path]
663:                         if now - self.last_trigger > self.debounce_ms:
664:                             self.last_trigger = now
665:                             yield path
666:                 
667:                 last_mtimes = current_mtimes
668:                 await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
669:                 
670:             except Exception as e:
671:                 print(f"File watcher error: {e}")
672:                 await asyncio.sleep(1)
673:     
674:     def start(self, callback):
675:         """Start the file watcher."""
676:         self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run_watcher(callback))
677:     
678:     async def _run_watcher(self, callback):
679:         """Run the watcher loop."""
680:         async for path in self.watch():
681:             await callback(path)
682:     
683:     async def stop(self):
684:         """Stop the file watcher."""
685:         self.running = False
686:         if self._task:
687:             self._task.cancel()
688:             try:
689:                 await self._task
690:             except asyncio.CancelledError:
691:                 pass

694: class HTTPServer:
695:     """Async HTTP server with SSE console streaming."""
696:     
697:     def __init__(self, port: int, directory: str, console_buffer: ConsoleBuffer, live_reload_server: LiveReloadServer):
698:         self.port = port
699:         self.directory = directory
700:         self.console_buffer = console_buffer
701:         self.live_reload_server = live_reload_server
702:         self.server: Optional[asyncio.Server] = None
703:         self.running = True

706:     async def handle_client(self, reader: asyncio.StreamReader, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter):
707:         """Handle incoming HTTP client request."""
708:         try:
709:             # Read request line
710:             request_line = await reader.readline()
711:             if not request_line:
712:                 writer.close()
713:                 await writer.wait_closed()
714:                 return
715:             
716:             request_line = request_line.decode().strip()
717:             
718:             # Parse request
719:             parts = request_line.split()
720:             if len(parts) < 2:
721:                 writer.close()
722:                 await writer.wait_closed()
723:                 return
724:             
725:             method = parts[0]
726:             path = parts[1]
727:             
728:             # Read headers
729:             headers = {}
730:             while True:
731:                 line = await reader.readline()
732:                 if not line or line == b'\r\n':
733:                     break
734:                 header = line.decode().strip()
735:                 if ':' in header:
736:                     key, value = header.split(':', 1)
737:                     headers[key.strip().lower()] = value.strip()
738:             
739:             # Route request
740:             if method == 'POST' and path == '/api/console/log':
741:                 await self.handle_console_log(reader, writer, headers)
742:             elif method == 'GET' and path == '/api/console/stream':
743:                 await self.handle_console_stream(reader, writer, headers)
744:             elif method == 'GET' and path == '/api/health':
745:                 await self.handle_health(writer)
746:             elif path.startswith('/api/cdp/'):
747:                 await self.handle_cdp(method, path, reader, writer, headers)
748:             else:
749:                 await self.handle_static(method, path, reader, writer, headers)
750:                 
751:         except Exception as e:
752:             print(f"Error handling client: {e}")
753:         finally:
754:             try:
755:                 writer.close()
756:                 await writer.wait_closed()
757:             except Exception:
758:                 pass
759:     
760:     async def handle_console_log(self, reader: asyncio.StreamReader, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter, headers: dict):
761:         """Handle POST /api/console/log - receive logs from browser."""
762:         content_length = int(headers.get('content-length', 0))
763:         body = await reader.read(content_length)
764:         
765:         try:
766:             log_data = json.loads(body.decode('utf-8'))
767:             
768:             # Handle batch logs
769:             if log_data.get('type') == 'console_batch' and 'logs' in log_data:
770:                 for entry in log_data['logs']:
771:                     if 'timestamp' not in entry:
772:                         entry['timestamp'] = datetime.now().isoformat()
773:                     self.console_buffer.append(entry)
774:             else:
775:                 # Individual log
776:                 if 'timestamp' not in log_data:
777:                     log_data['timestamp'] = datetime.now().isoformat()
778:                 self.console_buffer.append(log_data)
779:             
780:             # Send response
781:             writer.write(b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n')
782:             writer.write(b'Content-Type: application/json\r\n')
783:             writer.write(b'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *\r\n')
784:             writer.write(b'Connection: close\r\n')
785:             writer.write(b'\r\n')
786:             writer.write(json.dumps({"status": "received"}).encode())
787:             await writer.drain()
788:             
789:         except Exception as e:
790:             writer.write(b'HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request\r\n')
791:             writer.write(b'Content-Type: application/json\r\n')
792:             writer.write(b'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *\r\n')
793:             writer.write(b'Connection: close\r\n')
794:             writer.write(b'\r\n')
795:             writer.write(json.dumps({"error": "Invalid request"}).encode())
796:             await writer.drain()

798:     async def handle_console_stream(self, reader: asyncio.StreamReader, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter, headers: dict):
799:         """Handle GET /api/console/stream - SSE streaming endpoint."""
800:         # Send SSE headers
801:         writer.write(b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n')
802:         writer.write(b'Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8\r\n')
803:         writer.write(b'Cache-Control: no-cache\r\n')
804:         writer.write(b'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *\r\n')
805:         writer.write(b'Connection: keep-alive\r\n')
806:         writer.write(b'X-Accel-Buffering: no\r\n')
807:         writer.write(b'\r\n')
808:         await writer.drain()
809:         
810:         # Exponential backoff: 15s → 30s → 60s → 120s → max 300s
811:         base_interval = 15
812:         current_interval = base_interval
813:         max_interval = 300
814:         heartbeat_count = 0
815:         
816:         try:
817:             while self.running:
818:                 # Get buffered logs
819:                 logs = self.console_buffer.get_all()
820:                 
821:                 # Send buffered logs and reset exponential backoff
822:                 if logs:
823:                     current_interval = base_interval  # Reset to 15s
824:                     heartbeat_count = 0
825:                     
826:                     for log_entry in logs:
827:                         level = log_entry.get('level', 'log')
828:                         message = log_entry.get('message', '')
829:                         source = log_entry.get('source', 'browser')
830:                         formatted = format_log_entry(level, message, source)
831:                         writer.write(f"data: {formatted}\n\n".encode())
832:                         await writer.drain()
833:                 
834:                 # Send silent keepalive (SSE comment) to prevent connection timeout
835:                 heartbeat_count += 1
836:                 if heartbeat_count >= current_interval:
837:                     heartbeat_count = 0
838:                     writer.write(b': heartbeat\n\n')
839:                     await writer.drain()
840:                     # Exponential backoff
841:                     current_interval = min(current_interval * 2, max_interval)
842:                 
843:                 # Wait before next check
844:                 await asyncio.sleep(1)
845:                 
846:         except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, asyncio.CancelledError):
847:             pass
848:         finally:
849:             try:
850:                 writer.close()
851:                 await writer.wait_closed()
852:             except Exception:
853:                 pass

855:     async def handle_health(self, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter):
856:         """Handle GET /api/health - health check endpoint."""
857:         writer.write(b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n')
858:         writer.write(b'Content-Type: application/json\r\n')
859:         writer.write(b'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *\r\n')
860:         writer.write(b'Connection: close\r\n')
861:         writer.write(b'\r\n')
862:         writer.write(json.dumps({
863:             "status": "ok",
864:             "server": "p5.nvim asyncio",
865:             "console_buffer_size": len(self.console_buffer),
866:         }).encode())
867:         await writer.drain()

872:         if method == 'POST' and path == '/api/cdp/connect':
873:             await self.handle_cdp_connect(writer)

    if (!matcher.matches(*script.second)) continue;

    // in the script matcher.

    breakpointHints->setObject(breakpointId, std::move(hint));
  }

I've completed a thorough review of the CDP integration across `cdp.lua`, `server.lua`, `server.py`, `init.lua`, `commands.lua`, the inject scripts, tests, docs, and cross-checked against the official CDP spec and V8 source. Here's the full assessment.

---

# CDP Integration Assessment — p5.nvim

## 1. Architecture overview

The CDP stack is a 3-tier proxy:
- **`server.py`** — an asyncio HTTP server that also runs a `CDPClient` (raw `websockets` to Chrome's `/json` → `webSocketDebuggerUrl`). It translates CDP events into JSON lines on an NDJSON stream (`/api/cdp/stream`) and exposes HTTP endpoints (`connect`, `evaluate`, `debug/*`).
- **`lua/p5/cdp.lua`** — spawns Chrome, runs a `curl` SSE/NDJSON reader job, renders a 6-tab panel (Console/Network/Eval/Debug/Perf/Info), with a terminal fallback.
- **`lua/p5/server.lua`** — launches `server.py` and calls `cdp.open()`.

The layering itself is reasonable. The problems are in *what* each layer does and how the layers disagree.

## 2. Conformance against the official CDP spec — and where it breaks

### 2.1 FPS is fabricated (worst offender)
`server.py:243` hardcodes `perf_data = {'fps': 60}` in `_perf_loop`, and `_handle_perf` (`server.py:483-500`) looks up metrics named `FPS`, `DOMNodes`, `EventListeners`. **None of these exist** in the CDP Performance domain. Per the spec, `Performance.metrics` yields metrics named `Timestamp`, `Documents`, `Frames`, `JSEventListeners`, `Nodes`, `LayoutCount`, `JSHeapUsedSize`, etc. — there is no `FPS`, and the node/listener names are wrong (those are `Memory.getDOMCounters` names). So:
- FPS sparkline is a flat line of 60, always.
- Heap/nodes/listeners from the Performance event are always 0.
- There are **two competing sampling paths** (Performance domain events + a `Runtime.evaluate` polling loop `_perf_loop`) racing on the same Lua fields, so the displayed heap alternates between the `performance.memory` value and 0.

This is a "feature" that presents fake data as real diagnostics. Either compute FPS honestly (e.g. `requestAnimationFrame` counter via injected JS, or `Runtime.evaluate` `performance.now()` deltas between `Performance.metrics` events) or drop it.

### 2.2 Breakpoints are silently broken
`server.py:307-323` calls `Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl` with `url = "sketch.js"`. I verified in V8 source (`v8-debugger-agent-impl.cc`) that the matcher does:

```cpp
case BreakpointType::kByUrl:
  return script.sourceURL() == selector_;   // EXACT match
```

The script's `sourceURL()` is `http://localhost:8000/sketch.js`, so `url="sketch.js"` never matches. The `_scripts.get(url)` fallback (`Debugger.setBreakpoint` by scriptId) also keys on the *exact* URL, so it can't help either. Meanwhile the Lua side (`cdp.lua:330-335`) declares "Breakpoint set" on any HTTP 200 — but CDP returns success with an **empty `locations` array**. So the user sets a breakpoint, gets a green toast, and nothing ever pauses. This is the most user-hostile failure mode in the plugin: a silent no-op that looks successful.

### 2.3 Pause-highlight jump is broken by a string bug
`cdp.lua:788-789`:

```lua
local url_path = (url:match("://[^/]+(/.*)") or "/") .. (vim.fn.fnamemodify(url, ":t") or "")
local abs_path = project_root .. url_path:gsub("/$", "")
```

For `http://localhost:8000/sketch.js`: `url:match(...)` → `/sketch.js`, `fnamemodify(..., ":t")` → `sketch.js`, so `abs_path = cwd .. "/sketch.jssketch.js"`. The buffer lookup never matches, so "jump to the paused line" never fires. (Also `Debugger.CallFrame.url` is *deprecated* in the spec — the correct approach is resolving `location.scriptId` against your `scriptParsed` table, which the server already maintains.)

### 2.4 Correctly-implemented parts (for fairness)
- `Runtime.enable` / `Network.enable` / `Debugger.enable` / `Performance.enable` handshake on connect — spec-correct.
- `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` level mapping + args flattening + `stackTrace` handling (`server.py:386-418`) — spec-correct.
- `Runtime.exceptionThrown` handling — correct.
- `Network.requestWillBeSent`/`responseReceived`/`loadingFailed` pairing by `requestId` — correct event usage (minor: wall-clock duration deltas instead of `loadingFinished` timestamps; redirects leak `pending_requests`).
- `Runtime.evaluate` with `returnByValue` + `includeCommandLineAPI` — spec-correct.
- `Debugger.resume`/`stepOver`/`stepInto`/`stepOut` — spec-correct.

## 3. Loopholes & impracticalities

1. **Chrome launched without `--user-data-dir`** (`cdp.lua:112-120`). If *any* Chrome is already running, the new process with `--remote-debugging-port` just opens a tab in the existing instance and never exposes the debugging port. Connect then fails 5× with exponential backoff and a red dot. This is the single most common "why doesn't this work" trap and the fix is one flag.
2. **`remote_debugging_port` config is never forwarded to `server.py`** — `server.lua` passes only `--lr-*` flags; `server.py` hardcodes `CONFIG['cdp']['remote_debugging_port'] = 9222`. Configure 9333 and the server keeps dialing 9222. Silent, unreported.
3. **The CDP panel opens unconditionally on server start** (`server.lua:203-205`): `vim.defer_fn(function() pcall(cdp.open) end, 500)` — not gated on `cdp.enabled` or `autocmds.cdp_on_server_start`. Default config therefore pops the panel *and* auto-opens the browser, contradicting the documented opt-in behavior and fighting `auto_open_browser`.
4. **`cdp.enabled` is a lie** — `C.open`/`C.connect` auto-enable it on first use. The config knob has no effect; docs admit it ("auto-enabled when panel opens"). Either make it a real gate or remove it.
5. **Port drift on contention**: `server.py` binds `port + offset`, but `server.lua` stores the *requested* port (`S.port = port`). If 8000 is taken, the server runs on 8001 while all Lua requests target 8000. The server even prints the real port — Lua just never reads it.
6. **Eval entries stuck at "pending" forever** on network failure — `C.eval` has no `on_exit` handler, so a refused connection leaves the entry in limbo.
7. **Browser lifecycle is untracked** — closing the panel doesn't kill the launched Chrome; `browser_launched=false` on close causes the next open to spawn another Chrome (which, per #1, just opens a tab). No reuse, no cleanup.
8. **False-security eval filter** (`server.py:1008-1011`) — blocks `require(`, `process.env`, `global.`, `__dirname`, `file://`. This is Node-cargo-cult that runs in a browser context; it protects nothing (it's the user's own browser on localhost) and can't block anything real anyway. It gives a false sense of safety while rejecting harmless expressions.
9. **Double console instrumentation** — `assets/inject/console.js` rewrites `console.*` to fetch-POST `/api/console/log` on *every* page, *and* CDP `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` fires for the same call. While connected, the inject-POSTs pile up undrained in `console_buffer` and burst out on disconnect. Wasteful and confusing.
10. **No fallback ladder** — if Chrome is found but can't connect (profile conflict per #1), the user gets a disconnected dot with zero guidance instead of falling back to the terminal console or an actionable error.

## 4. Unusable / redundant features

**Broken (presented as working):**
- FPS/sparkline (fake), breakpoints (never resolve), pause-line jump (string bug), canvas_state (never populated), perf `r` recording toggle (label only — data keeps flowing), `_terminal_auto_clear` (always trims since `last_error` is never written).

**Dead code:**
- `handle_cdp_network_clear` endpoint — defined *and* unit-tested, but **not routed** in `handle_cdp`; Lua's `network_clear` only clears local state.
- `_terminal_reconnect` — never called.
- `Timeline.eventRecorded → pass` branch, `_perf_loop` vs `Performance.metrics` duplication, deprecated `/api/console/stream` + inject console retained alongside CDP.
- `Pending requests`/`_scripts` never pruned.

**Features actually worth adding when debugging sketches** (my honest opinion, highest-value first):
1. **Pause-aware REPL** — when paused, route eval through `Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame(topFrameId)` so you can inspect locals, not just the paused global scope.
2. **Scope/locals panel** — `Debugger.paused` already carries `callFrames[].scopeChain`; render locals via `Runtime.getProperties`. The current Debug tab shows a call stack and nothing to actually inspect.
3. **Pause-on-exception toggle** (`Debugger.setPauseOnExceptions` uncaught/all) — the single most useful thing for hunting sketch runtime errors.
4. **`Page.reload`** — pairs with live reload; currently there's no in-panel way to restart the sketch.
5. **`Page.captureScreenshot`** — a sketch is visual; grabbing the canvas and opening it in nvim beats guessing.
6. **Breakpoint from the sketch buffer** — click/set a sign on a line in `sketch.js`; server resolves the filename to the exact `sourceURL` via its `_scripts` map (this also fixes §2.2).
7. **Real memory metrics** — `Memory.getDOMCounters` for nodes/listeners, `Performance.getMetrics` for heap; drop the `Runtime.evaluate` polling.

## 5. Keybinding review — does it respect Neovim defaults?

The panel is a `nofile`, `nomodifiable` scratch buffer, so buffer-local mappings are *contained*. But:

- **`1`–`6` are the real problem.** They override Vim's count prefixes. `3j` inside the panel doesn't move down 3 lines — it switches to the Eval tab. That's a direct violation of core Vim grammar and the strongest argument against the current scheme.
- **Operator/command clobbering**: `s` (substitute), `c` (change), `x` (delete char), `b` (word-back), `r` (replace), `f` (find), `i`, `o` (operators), `D` (delete-to-EOL), `K` (manpage), `J` (join), `/` (search). Even in a read-only HUD, this trains users into a private "language" that doesn't transfer and tripped-up muscle memory is inevitable (`K` → manpage, `J` → join are universal).
- `q`/`<Esc>` to close is good and conventional for scratch buffers. `j/k/gg/G/zz` kept as motions is good. `<LeftMouse>` tab-clicking is a nice touch.

**My verdict**: not intuitive enough. The fix is to treat this buffer as a *HUD with a documented mapping table*, but:
- Tab switching should move off bare digits — e.g. `g1`..`g6` or `gt`/`gT`-style, keeping `1`-`6` as counts.
- Drop `s/x/c/b/r/f/i/o/D/K/J` conflicts; use mnemonic *pairs* where possible and keep them only on tabs where they're meaningful (`n`/`N` step? `p` pause?, etc.) or scope them to a `<leader>`/`[`/`]` prefix.
- The terminal fallback remapping `q`/`c`/`<C-c>` in a *real terminal buffer* is more intrusive — those buffers may be interactive; consider guarding or documenting.

## 6. Recommended fix plan (proposed, in priority order)

1. **Launch + connect correctness** — dedicated temp `--user-data-dir`, `--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1`, poll `/json/version` for readiness, propagate actual port. Add `--cdp-port` to `server.py` config parsing and pass it from `server.lua`.
2. **Gate `cdp.open()` on `cdp.enabled`** (or the autocmd), removing the unconditional auto-open; make `cdp.enabled` a real gate or delete it.
3. **Fix breakpoints** — resolve bare filenames against the server's `scriptParsed` URL map, use exact `sourceURL` with `setBreakpointByUrl` or `scriptId` with `setBreakpoint`; return `locations` length; report "resolved at N locations" vs "no matching script" to the user.
4. **Fix `_highlight_paused` URL→path mapping**; drive it from `location.scriptId` → server-resolved file, not deprecated `url`.
5. **Honest perf** — use `Performance.getMetrics` + `Memory.getDOMCounters`, compute FPS from real timestamps or drop it; delete `_perf_loop`.
6. **Single console path** — disable the inject `console.js` rewrite when CDP is connected (or gate on a status flag); drain `console_buffer` for the terminal fallback.
7. **Pause-aware eval** (`Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame`) + scope rendering + `setPauseOnExceptions` + `Page.reload`/`Page.captureScreenshot` — replaces the dead/weak features.
8. **Keybinding cleanup** per §5.
9. **Prune dead code** — unroute-able `handle_cdp_network_clear` (wire it or delete), `_terminal_reconnect`, `last_error` trim, `canvas_state`, `Timeline.eventRecorded`, `recording` toggle, redundant endpoints.
10. **Graceful fallback ladder** — Chrome absent → terminal console (exists); Chrome present but connect fails → actionable error + offer terminal fallback.
11. **Tests** — several tests currently *codify the bugs* (`set_breakpoint('sketch.js:42')` asserts the wrong URL is sent; FPS/perf tests assert the fake data). They must be updated to assert spec-correct behavior, and new tests added for the above.

Full hardening it is, with HUD keymaps kept-but-documented and the inject console retained as a deduped fallback. Here's the implementation plan.

## Implementation plan

### A. `server.py`
1. **Config plumbing** — add `--cdp-port` to `_parse_config`; drive `CONFIG['cdp']['remote_debugging_port']` from it.
2. **Honest performance** — rewrite `_handle_perf` to map real Performance-domain metric names: `JSHeapUsedSize`→heap, `Nodes`→nodes, `JSEventListeners`→listeners, and compute **FPS from the `Frames` counter delta** between `Performance.metrics` events (~1/s cadence). Delete the fake `fps: 60` fallback and the entire `_perf_loop` (`Runtime.evaluate` polling) — the Performance domain already emits the data.
3. **Breakpoints** — `set_breakpoint`: resolve bare filenames against `_scripts` (exact-URL → scriptId); if matched, use `Debugger.setBreakpoint` by scriptId; else `Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl` with the resolved exact `sourceURL`. Return `{ resolved = #locations, breakpointId }` so the UI can report honestly instead of "set" on an empty `locations`.
4. **New CDP features (genuinely useful for sketches)**:
   - `Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame` — track last paused `callFrameId`; `/api/cdp/evaluate` routes through it when paused (locals inspection), else `Runtime.evaluate`.
   - `/api/cdp/debug/pause` (`Debugger.pause`), `/api/cdp/debug/pauseExceptions` (`Debugger.setPauseOnExceptions`), `/api/cdp/page/reload` (`Page.reload`), `/api/cdp/page/screenshot` (`Page.captureScreenshot`, base64).
5. **Wire `/api/cdp/network` DELETE** (currently-routed-nowhere `handle_cdp_network_clear`) into `handle_cdp`; keep behavior.
6. **Prune** `Timeline.eventRecorded` branch; clear `pending_requests` on disconnect.
7. **Console dedupe** — `inject_scripts` embeds `window.__P5_CDP_ACTIVE` (connect state at serve time); `console.js` also re-checks once via `/api/cdp/status`; only rewrites `console.*` when CDP is *not* active. Graceful: on fetch failure, fall back to rewriting.

### B. `lua/p5/cdp.lua`
1. **Launch correctness** — add `--user-data-dir=<tempdir>` (track it) and `--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1`; clean up tempdir on close; new config `cdp.close_browser_on_close` (default true) to kill our dedicated instance.
2. **Fix `_highlight_paused`** — replace the broken URL concatenation with basename matching against open buffers (`nvim_buf_get_name` tail vs `url` tail).
3. **Eval stuck-"pending"** — add `on_exit` to `C.eval`'s request marking entries failed.
4. **Recording toggle becomes real** — when `recording` is off, stop appending perf samples (display-side gate).
5. **New commands** — `C.pause`, `C.pause_on_exceptions`, `C.reload`, `C.screenshot`, bound to documented keys; Debug tab shows pause-exception state and resolved-breakpoint feedback.
6. **`network_clear`/`D`** — call `DELETE /api/cdp/network` (server-side clear) *and* clear local.
7. **`_terminal_auto_clear`** — remove the always-true trim (relies on the never-written `last_error`); keep manual `c` clear.
8. **`_terminal_reconnect`** — actually wire it into termopen `on_exit` (exit != 0) so the existing retry logic runs.
9. **`C.open` guard** — if `state.win` already valid, focus instead of spawning a duplicate panel.
10. **Keymaps** — keep the current HUD table unchanged; add an opt-out (`cdp.keymaps = false` skips `_set_keymaps`); document new keys.

### C. `lua/p5/server.lua`
1. Gate `vim.defer_fn(pcall(cdp.open), 500)` on `cdp.config.enabled` (and/or the autocmd) — stops the unconditional panel pop.
2. Pass `--cdp-port <n>` to `server.py`.
3. Capture the **actual bound port** from server stdout (`Server running at http://localhost:<real>/`) and update `S.port`, fixing the port-drift mismatch.

### D. `lua/p5/init.lua`
- Config additions: `cdp.keymaps = true`, `cdp.close_browser_on_close = true`; document `cdp.enabled` as the gate for server auto-open.

### E. `assets/inject/console.js`
- Status-aware rewrite per A.7.

### F. `lua/p5/commands.lua`
- Route `network_clear` through the server; add completions for `pause`, `pauseExceptions`, `reload`, `screenshot`.

### G. Docs
- `README.md` + `doc/p5-nvim.txt`: document the keymap table as **HUD-only** (with opt-out), honest perf semantics, new commands, and a troubleshooting entry for the Chrome-profile/`--user-data-dir` fix.

### H. Tests
- `test_cdp_client.py`: update breakpoint test to expect scriptId/exact-URL resolution; rewrite perf tests around real metric names + `Frames`-delta FPS; add tests for the new endpoints, `--cdp-port` parsing, network-clear routing, and evaluateOnCallFrame routing when paused.
- `cdp_spec.lua`: eval `on_exit`, highlight mapping, keymaps opt-out, open guard, network_clear endpoint call, terminal-reconnect wiring.
- Remove tests that currently *codify the bugs* (the `url='sketch.js'` assertion and fake-FPS assertions).

Ready to execute this once you approve. One note: the keymap "keep but document" choice means the `1`–`6` count-shadowing stays — I'll document it explicitly as a HUD-only caveat, but I'd still recommend `g1`-`g6` eventually if it bites anyone.

def _resolve_script(self, name):
        """Find scriptId for a bare filename (exact match or URL basename)."""
        if not name:
            return None
        if name in self._scripts:
            return self._scripts[name]
        tail = name.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]
        for url, sid in self._scripts.items():
            if url.rsplit('/', 1)[-1] == tail:
                return sid
        return None

    async def evaluate(self, expression: str):
        if self._paused_frame_id:
            return await self.send_command('Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame', {
                'callFrameId': self._paused_frame_id,
                'expression': expression,
                'returnByValue': True,
                'includeCommandLineAPI': True,
            })
        return await self.send_command('Runtime.evaluate', {
            'expression': expression,
            'returnByValue': True,
            'includeCommandLineAPI': True,
        })

    async def set_breakpoint(self, location: str):
        parts = location.rsplit(':', 1)
        if len(parts) != 2:
            raise ValueError("Use format: file.js:line")
        url, line = parts[0], int(parts[1])
        sid = self._resolve_script(url)
        if sid:
            result = await self.send_command('Debugger.setBreakpoint', {
                'location': {'scriptId': sid, 'lineNumber': line - 1},
            })
            result['resolved'] = 1 if result.get('actualLocation') else 0
            return result
        result = await self.send_command('Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl', {
            'url': url,
            'lineNumber': line - 1,
        })
        result['resolved'] = len(result.get('locations', []))
        return result

    async def resume(self):
        await self.send_command('Debugger.resume')

    async def step_over(self):
        await self.send_command('Debugger.stepOver')

    async def step_into(self):
        await self.send_command('Debugger.stepInto')

async def handle_cdp_debug_pause(self, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter):
        if not self.cdp_client or not self.cdp_client.connected:
            await self._json_error(writer, 503, 'CDP not connected')
            return
        try:
            await self.cdp_client.pause()
            await self._json_response(writer, {'status': 'pausing'})
        except Exception as e:
            await self._json_error(writer, 400, str(e))

    async def handle_cdp_debug_pause_exceptions(self, reader: asyncio.StreamReader, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter, headers: dict):
        if not self.cdp_client or not self.cdp_client.connected:
            await self._json_error(writer, 503, 'CDP not connected')
            return
        content_length = int(headers.get('content-length', 0))
        body = await reader.read(content_length)
        try:
            data = json.loads(body.decode())
            state = data.get('state', 'none')
            await self.cdp_client.set_pause_on_exceptions(state)
            await self._json_response(writer, {'status': 'pause_on_exceptions=' + state})
        except Exception as e:
            await self._json_error(writer, 400, str(e))

    async def handle_cdp_page_reload(self, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter):
        if not self.cdp_client or not self.cdp_client.connected:
            await self._json_error(writer, 503, 'CDP not connected')
            return
        try:
            await self.cdp_client.reload_page()
            await self._json_response(writer, {'status': 'reloading'})
        except Exception as e:
            await self._json_error(writer, 400, str(e))

    async def handle_cdp_page_screenshot(self, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter):
        if not self.cdp_client or not self.cdp_client.connected:
            await self._json_error(writer, 503, 'CDP not connected')
            return
        try:
            result = await self.cdp_client.capture_screenshot()
            await self._json_response(writer, result)
        except Exception as e:
            await self._json_error(writer, 400, str(e))

    async def handle_cdp_network_clear(self, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter):
        if self.cdp_client:
            self.cdp_client.clear_network_log()
        await self._json_response(writer, {'status': 'cleared'})

content.text:
## Goal
- Harden the p5.nvim CDP integration against the official Chrome DevTools Protocol spec: fix fake broken features (FPS, breakpoints, pause-highlight), prune dead code, add useful debugging capabilities, document HUD keymaps, and commit/push each phase.

## Constraints & Preferences
- User approved "All of it (full hardening)" — fixes 1–11 from the assessment.
- Keymaps: **Keep but document** — keep current HUD keymap table (incl. `1`–`6` tab switch), add opt-out config, document as HUD-only.
- Console: **Keep inject-based console as fallback, dedupe** — stop double instrumentation when CDP is active.
- Commit each phase when done and push when done.

## Progress
### Done
- Full assessment done (CDP conformance, loopholes, keybindings, fix plan) — presented and approved.
- **Phase A (`server.py`) — partial:**
  - `_parse_config`: added `--cdp-port` flag → `cfg['cdp']['remote_debugging_port']`.
  - `CDPClient.__init__`: replaced `_perf_metrics`/`_perf_task` with `_paused_frame_id` and `_perf_prev` (Frames-delta).
  - Deleted fake `_perf_loop` (Runtime.evaluate polling) entirely; removed `_perf_task` cancel from `disconnect`; added `pending_requests.clear()` + `_paused_frame_id=None` on disconnect.
  - `evaluate`: routes via `Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame` when `_paused_frame_id` set, else `Runtime.evaluate`.
  - `set_breakpoint`: `_resolve_script()` matches bare filename → exact URL in `_scripts` or URL-basename match → `Debugger.setBreakpoint` by scriptId; else `setBreakpointByUrl` with exact URL; sets `result['resolved']` = 0/1 (scriptId path) or `len(locations)` (URL path).
  - New CDPClient methods: `pause`, `set_pause_on_exceptions(state)`, `reload_page`, `capture_screenshot`.
  - `_handle_perf` rewritten with real metric names: `JSHeapUsedSize`→heap, `Nodes`→nodes, `JSEventListeners`→listeners, `Frames` cumulative counter delta per ~1s event → real FPS (clamped 0–1000); removed `_perf_metrics.append`.
  - `_handle_paused`: now stores `self._paused_frame_id = frames_raw[0].get('callFrameId')` and adds `scriptId` to per-frame dicts.
  - Removed dead `Timeline.eventRecorded: pass` branch; merged `Debugger.resumed` handler to also clear `_paused_frame_id` (fixed a duplicated unreachable elif).
  - `handle_cdp` routing: added `POST /api/cdp/debug/pause`, `POST /api/cdp/debug/pauseExceptions`, `POST /api/cdp/page/reload`, `GET /api/cdp/page/screenshot`, and wired `DELETE /api/cdp/network` (the previously unrouted `handle_cdp_network_clear`).
  - `HTTPServer` handlers added: `handle_cdp_debug_pause`, `handle_cdp_debug_pause_exceptions`, `handle_cdp_page_reload`, `handle_cdp_page_screenshot`; existing `handle_cdp_network_clear` retained as the DELETE handler.

### In Progress
- Phase A (`server.py`) — remaining items: console dedupe via inject scripts/status (server-side part), verify remaining `_perf_metrics` references are gone, run pytest.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Key Decisions
- FPS computed honestly from `Performance.metrics` `Frames` counter delta (matches CDP spec) instead of fake `fps: 60`.
- Breakpoints resolved client-side (server) against `scriptParsed` URL map for exact `sourceURL`/scriptId — fixes V8 exact-match `setBreakpointByUrl` failure confirmed in `v8-debugger-agent-impl.cc`.
- Pause-aware eval via `Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame` top frame.
- Keep current HUD keymap table per user choice; add `cdp.keymaps` opt-out + docs only.
- Inject console stays as no-Chrome fallback; dedupe when CDP active.

## Next Steps
1. Finish `server.py` Phase A: console dedupe (embed CDP-active state; console.js checks `/api/cdp/status` and skips rewriting when connected), confirm no stale `_perf_metrics` refs, run `pytest` (update `tests/test_cdp_client.py` first — breakpoint/perf tests encode old buggy behavior).
2. Commit Phase A; push.
3. Phase B `lua/p5/cdp.lua`: Chrome `--user-data-dir` + `--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1` + tempdir cleanup; fix `_highlight_paused` basename matching (broken `url_path` concatenation bug); eval `on_exit` marks pending failure; recording toggle gates samples; new commands (pause, pauseExceptions, reload, screenshot); wire network_clear to DELETE endpoint; wire `_terminal_reconnect`; remove always-true `_terminal_auto_clear`; open guard for existing win; `cdp.keymaps=false` opt-out.
4. Commit Phase B; push.
5. Phase C `lua/p5/server.lua`: gate `cdp.open()` on `cdp.config.enabled`; pass `--cdp-port`; capture actual bound port from stdout (fixes port-drift mismatch).
6. Phase D `lua/p5/init.lua`: add `cdp.keymaps`, `cdp.close_browser_on_close` config; document.
7. Phase E `assets/inject/console.js`: status-aware console.* rewrite.
8. Phase F `lua/p5/commands.lua`: route network_clear via server; new subcommand completions.
9. Phase G docs (README.md + doc/p5-nvim.txt): HUD keymap table as HUD-only, new commands, troubleshooting for Chrome profile/`--user-data-dir`.
10. Phase H tests: update `tests/test_cdp_client.py` and `tests/p5/cdp_spec.lua` to spec-correct expectations; run pytest + luacheck/stylua; final commit + push.

## Critical Context
- **V8 fact**: `Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl` `url` matches script `sourceURL()` EXACTLY (`script.sourceURL() == selector_` in `v8-debugger-agent-impl.cc`), so old `url="sketch.js"` never resolved against `http://localhost:8000/sketch.js`.
- Chrome launch without `--user-data-dir` fails to expose debug port if an existing Chrome instance is running — the top user-facing launch bug.
- `server.py` port-drift: binds `port + offset` on contention but Lua stores requested port.
- Old `_highlight_paused` bug: `url:match("://[^/]+(/.*)") .. fnamemodify(url,":t")` double-appends basename → `sketch.jssketch.js`.
- `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` + inject console.js double-instrumentation: console.js fetch-POSTs to `/api/console/log` never drained while CDP connected.
- Duplicate-elif bug in `_message_loop` fixed (two `Debugger.resumed` branches; second was unreachable).
- `handle_cdp_network_clear` was defined + unit-tested but never routed.

## Relevant Files
- `server.py`: CDP client + HTTP proxy; Phase A changes (config, perf, breakpoints, new endpoints).
- `lua/p5/cdp.lua`: Lua CDP panel, keymaps, terminal fallback; Phase B target.
- `lua/p5/server.lua`: server launcher; Phase C target (gate, --cdp-port, port capture).
- `lua/p5/init.lua`: config (add `cdp.keymaps`, `cdp.close_browser_on_close`).
- `lua/p5/commands.lua`: `:P5 cdp` subcommands (network_clear routing, new completions).
- `assets/inject/console.js`: console rewrite fallback; needs CDP-status dedupe.
- `assets/inject/livereload.js`: unaffected.
- `tests/test_cdp_client.py`: Python CDP tests — encode old buggy breakpoint/perf/etc.; must be updated.
- `tests/p5/cdp_spec.lua`: Lua CDP specs — must be updated (eval on_exit, highlight, opt-outs).
- `README.md`, `doc/p5-nvim.txt`: docs for Phase G.
Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification if you are unsure how to proceed.

664: C._start_sse_job = function()
665: 	if C.state.job_id then
666: 		return
667: 	end
668: 	if not check_curl() then
669: 		return
670: 	end
671: 	local url = string.format("http://localhost:%d/api/cdp/stream", C.state.port)
672: 	C.state.job_id = vim.fn.jobstart({ "curl", "-s", "-N", "--max-time", "3600", url }, {
673: 		on_stdout = function(_, data)
674: 			if not data then
675: 				return
676: 			end
677: 			local buf = C.state.sse_buffer or ""
678: 			for _, chunk in ipairs(data) do
679: 				buf = buf .. (chunk or "")
680: 			end
681: 			local lines = vim.split(buf, "\n", { plain = true })
682: 			C.state.sse_buffer = table.remove(lines) or ""
683: 			for _, line in ipairs(lines) do
684: 				if line ~= "" then
685: 					local ok, ev = pcall(vim.json.decode, line)
686: 					if ok then
687: 						vim.schedule(function()
688: 							C._on_event(ev)
689: 						end)
690: 					end
691: 				end
692: 			end
693: 		end,
694: 		on_exit = function()
695: 			vim.schedule(function()
696: 				C.state.job_id = nil
697: 				C.state.sse_buffer = ""
698: 				if C.state.buf and is_buf(C.state.buf) and C.state.connected then
699: 					notify("CDP stream disconnected, reconnecting...", "info")
700: 					vim.defer_fn(function()
701: 						C._start_sse_job()
702: 					end, 1000)
703: 				end
704: 			end)
705: 		end,
706: 	})
707: end

709: C._on_event = function(data)
710: 	local t = data.type
711: 	if t == "console" then
712: 		local cd = C.tab_data.console
713: 		table.insert(cd, data)
714: 		if #cd > 1000 then
715: 			table.remove(cd, 1)
716: 		end
717: 		if C.state.active_tab == 1 then
718: 			C.render_all()
719: 		end
720: 	elseif t == "network" then
721: 		local nd = C.tab_data.network
722: 		table.insert(nd, data)
723: 		if #nd > 500 then
724: 			table.remove(nd, 1)
725: 		end
726: 		if C.state.active_tab == 2 then
727: 			C.render_all()
728: 		end
729: 	elseif t == "debugger" then
730: 		C.tab_data.debugger = data
731: 		if data.event == "paused" then
732: 			local frames = data.callFrames or {}
733: 			if #frames > 0 then
734: 				C._highlight_paused(frames[1].url, frames[1].line)
735: 			end
736: 		elseif data.event == "resumed" then
737: 			C._clear_debug_highlights()
738: 		end
739: 		if C.state.active_tab == 4 then
740: 			C.render_all()
741: 		end
742: 	elseif t == "perf" then
743: 		local pd = C.tab_data.perf
744: 		if data.fps then
745: 			table.insert(pd.fps, data.fps)
746: 			if #pd.fps > 100 then
747: 				table.remove(pd.fps, 1)
748: 			end
749: 		end
750: 		if data.heap then
751: 			pd.heap = data.heap
752: 		end
753: 		if data.nodes then
754: 			pd.nodes = data.nodes
755: 		end
756: 		if data.listeners then
757: 			pd.listeners = data.listeners
758: 		end
759: 		if C.state.active_tab == 5 then
760: 			C.render_all()
761: 		end
762: 	elseif t == "status" then
763: 		local was_connected = C.state.connected
764: 		C.state.connected = (data.state == "connected")
765: 		C.state.page_url = data.url or ""
766: 		if was_connected and not C.state.connected and C.state.buf and is_buf(C.state.buf) then
767: 			if C.state.mode == "panel" then
768: 				notify("CDP disconnected, reconnecting...", "info")
769: 				vim.defer_fn(function()
770: 					if C.state.buf and is_buf(C.state.buf) then
771: 						C.connect()
772: 					end
773: 				end, 1000)
774: 			end
775: 		end
776: 		if C.state.buf and is_buf(C.state.buf) then
777: 			C.render_all()
778: 		end
779: 	end
780: end

782: C._highlight_paused = function(url, line)

784: 	if not url or not line then

787: 	local project_root = vim.fn.getcwd()
788: 	local url_path = (url:match("://[^/]+(/.*)") or "/") .. (vim.fn.fnamemodify(url, ":t") or "")
789: 	local abs_path = project_root .. url_path:gsub("/$", "")
790: 	for _, buf in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_bufs()) do
791: 		local name = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(buf)
792: 		if name == abs_path then

794: 				sign_text = "●",
795: 				sign_hl_group = "P5CDPDebugSign",

803: 			pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor, 0, { line, 0 })

807: 	end

816: C._fetch_lsp_symbols = function()
817: 	C.tab_data.info.symbols = {}
818: 	local bufnr
819: 	for _, b in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_bufs()) do
820: 		if vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(b):match("sketch%.js$") then
821: 			bufnr = b
822: 			break
823: 		end
824: 	end
825: 	bufnr = bufnr or vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
826: 	if not bufnr then
827: 		return
828: 	end
829: 	local clients = vim.lsp.get_clients({ bufnr = bufnr })
830: 	if #clients == 0 then
831: 		return
832: 	end
833: 	local ok, result = pcall(vim.lsp.buf_request_sync, bufnr, "textDocument/documentSymbol", {
834: 		textDocument = { uri = vim.uri_from_bufnr(bufnr) },
835: 	}, 1000)
836: 	if not ok or not result then
837: 		return
838: 	end
839: 	for _, res in ipairs(result) do
840: 		if res.result then
841: 			local function flatten(symbols, depth)
842: 				depth = depth or 0
843: 				for _, sym in ipairs(symbols) do
844: 					local kind_name = ({
845: 						"File",
846: 						"Module",
847: 						"Namespace",
848: 						"Package",
849: 						"Class",
850: 						"Method",
851: 						"Property",
852: 						"Field",
853: 						"Constructor",
854: 						"Enum",
855: 						"Interface",
856: 						"Function",
857: 						"Variable",
858: 						"Constant",
859: 						"String",
860: 						"Number",
861: 						"Boolean",
862: 						"Array",
863: 						"Object",
864: 						"Key",
865: 						"Null",
866: 						"EnumMember",
867: 						"Struct",
868: 						"Event",
869: 						"Operator",
870: 						"TypeParameter",
871: 					})[sym.kind] or "Unknown"
872: 					local icon = ({
873: 						Method = "ƒ",
874: 						Function = "ƒ",
875: 						Variable = "◆",
876: 						Constant = "◇",
877: 						Class = "○",
878: 						Property = "●",
879: 						Field = "●",
880: 					})[kind_name] or "·"
881: 					table.insert(C.tab_data.info.symbols, {
882: 						name = sym.name,
883: 						kind = kind_name,
884: 						icon = icon,
885: 						depth = depth,
886: 						lnum = (sym.range or {}).start and sym.range.start.line + 1 or 0,
887: 					})
888: 					if sym.children then
889: 						flatten(sym.children, depth + 1)
890: 					end
891: 				end
892: 			end
893: 			if type(res.result) == "table" then
894: 				flatten(res.result)
895: 			end
896: 		end
897: 	end
898: end

959: 	local tab_line = lines[1] or ""
960: 	for _, tab in ipairs(tabs) do
961: 		local pattern = string.format("▎%d:%s", tab.key, tab.name)
962: 		local start_idx = tab_line:find(pattern, 1, true)
963: 		if start_idx then
964: 			vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, "P5CDPActiveTab", 0, start_idx - 1, start_idx - 1 + #pattern)
965: 		else
966: 			local raw = string.format(" %d:%s", tab.key, tab.name)
967: 			local raw_start = tab_line:find(raw, 1, true)
968: 			if raw_start then
969: 				vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, "P5CDPTab", 0, raw_start - 1, raw_start - 1 + #raw)
970: 			end
971: 		end
972: 	end
973: 	local close_start = tab_line:find("[X]", 1, true)
974: 	if close_start then
975: 		vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, "P5CDPClose", 0, close_start - 1, close_start + 2)
976: 	end
977: 	local connected_dot = tab_line:find("●", 1, true)
978: 	if connected_dot then
979: 		local hl = C.state.connected and "P5CDPConnected" or "P5CDPDisconnected"
980: 		vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, hl, 0, connected_dot - 1, connected_dot)
981: 	end
982: 	local k = C.state.active_tab
983: 	for ln = 3, #lines do
984: 		local l = lines[ln] or ""

990: 				vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, "P5CDPConsoleWarn", ln - 1, 0, -1)
991: 			elseif level == "INFO" then
992: 				vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, "P5CDPConsoleInfo", ln - 1, 0, -1)

994: 				vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, "P5CDPConsoleLog", ln - 1, 0, -1)

997: 			local status = l:match("^%s+(%d+)")
998: 			if status then
999: 				local first = status:sub(1, 1)
1000: 				local hl = ({
1001: 					["2"] = "P5CDPNetwork2xx",

1003: 					["4"] = "P5CDPNetwork4xx",
1004: 					["5"] = "P5CDPNetwork5xx",

1007: 					local _, s = l:find("^%s+%S+%s+")
1008: 					if s then
1009: 						vim.api.nvim_buf_add_highlight(buf, -1, hl, ln - 1, s, s + #status)
1010: 					end
1011: 				end
1012: 			end
1013: 		elseif k == 3 then
1014: 			if l:match("^%s+←") then

1058: C._render_console = function()
1059: 	local data = C.tab_data.console
1060: 	local filter = C.state.console_filter or "all"
1061: 	local search = C.state.search or ""
1062: 	if #data == 0 then
1063: 		return { " No console output yet" }
1064: 	end
1065: 	local lines = {}
1066: 	for _, entry in ipairs(data) do
1067: 		if filter ~= "all" and entry.level ~= filter then
1068: 			goto continue
1069: 		end
1070: 		local ts = entry.timestamp or ""
1071: 		local lvl = (entry.level or "log"):upper():sub(1, 5)
1072: 		local msg = entry.message or ""
1073: 		if search ~= "" and not msg:lower():find(search:lower(), 1, true) then
1074: 			goto continue
1075: 		end
1076: 		local line = string.format(" [%s] %s %s", ts, lvl, msg)
1077: 		table.insert(lines, line)
1078: 		if entry.stack and #entry.stack > 0 then
1079: 			for _, frame in ipairs(entry.stack) do
1080: 				local floc = string.format("   at %s (%s:%d:%d)", frame["function"], frame.url, frame.line, frame.column)
1081: 				table.insert(lines, floc)
1082: 			end
1083: 		end
1084: 		::continue::
1085: 	end
1086: 	if #lines == 0 then
1087: 		table.insert(lines, ' (no matches for filter "' .. filter .. '")')
1088: 	end
1089: 	return lines
1090: end

1187: C._render_performance = function()
1188: 	local pd = C.tab_data.perf
1189: 	local lines = {}
1190: 	local rec = pd.recording
1191: 	table.insert(lines, string.format(" Recording: %s", rec and "● ON" or "○ OFF"))
1192: 	table.insert(lines, string.rep("─", 30))
1193: 	local fps = pd.fps
1194: 	local avg1 = 0
1195: 	local avg10 = 0
1196: 	local latest = fps[#fps] or 0
1197: 	if #fps > 0 then
1198: 		local sum1, sum10 = 0, 0
1199: 		local n1 = math.min(#fps, 1)
1200: 		local n10 = math.min(#fps, 10)
1201: 		for i = #fps - n1 + 1, #fps do
1202: 			if i >= 1 then
1203: 				sum1 = sum1 + fps[i]
1204: 			end
1205: 		end
1206: 		for i = #fps - n10 + 1, #fps do
1207: 			if i >= 1 then
1208: 				sum10 = sum10 + fps[i]
1209: 			end
1210: 		end
1211: 		avg1 = n1 > 0 and math.floor(sum1 / n1) or 0
1212: 		avg10 = n10 > 0 and math.floor(sum10 / n10) or 0
1213: 	end
1214: 	table.insert(lines, string.format(" FPS:      %d (1s: %d | 10s: %d)", latest, avg1, avg10))
1215: 	local spark = {}
1216: 	local bars = { "▁", "▂", "▃", "▄", "▅", "▆", "▇", "█" }
1217: 	local window = 20
1218: 	local recent = {}
1219: 	for i = math.max(1, #fps - window + 1), #fps do
1220: 		table.insert(recent, fps[i])
1221: 	end
1222: 	local max_fps = 60
1223: 	for _, v in ipairs(recent) do
1224: 		local idx = math.min(math.floor((v / max_fps) * #bars) + 1, #bars)
1225: 		table.insert(spark, bars[idx])
1226: 	end
1227: 	if #spark > 0 then
1228: 		table.insert(lines, " FPS trend: " .. table.concat(spark, ""))
1229: 	end
1230: 	table.insert(lines, "")
1231: 	table.insert(lines, string.format(" JS Heap:  %.1f MB", pd.heap / 1048576))
1232: 	table.insert(lines, string.format(" DOM nodes: %d", pd.nodes))
1233: 	table.insert(lines, string.format(" Listeners: %d", pd.listeners))
1234: 	table.insert(lines, "")
1235: 	table.insert(lines, " Keymaps:")
1236: 	table.insert(lines, "   r     toggle recording")
1237: 	table.insert(lines, "   c     clear metrics")
1238: 	return lines
1239: end

1280: C._open_terminal = function()
1281: 	local has_snacks, snacks = pcall(require, "snacks")
1282: 	C.state.mode = "terminal"
1283: 	local t = C.state.terminal
1284: 	t.connected = false

1288: 	local pos = C.config.view.position or "below"
1289: 	local height = C.config.view.height or math.floor(vim.o.lines * 0.3)
1290: 	local split_cmd = core.split_cmd[pos] or core.split_cmd.below
1291: 
1292: 	if has_snacks then
1293: 		local term = snacks.terminal({ "curl", "-s", "-N", url }, {
1294: 			win = {
1295: 				title = "p5-console",
1296: 				---@diagnostic disable-next-line: assign-type-mismatch
1297: 				position = pos == "below" and "bottom" or pos,
1298: 				size = height,
1299: 			},
1300: 			auto_close = false,
1301: 			scrollback = 1000,
1302: 			interactive = false,
1303: 			keys = {
1304: 				q = "hide",
1305: 				["<C-c>"] = "hide",
1306: 				j = "scroll_down",
1307: 				k = "scroll_up",
1308: 				G = "scroll_to_bottom",
1309: 				gg = "scroll_to_top",
1310: 				["<C-d>"] = "page_down",
1311: 				["<C-u>"] = "page_up",
1312: 			},
1313: 		})
1314: 		C.state.win = term.win
1315: 		C.state.buf = term.buf
1316: 		disable_term_mode(C.state.buf)
1317: 		C._terminal_auto_clear()
1318: 		return
1319: 	end

1321: 	-- Manual terminal fallback (no snacks)
1322: 	vim.cmd(split_cmd:format(height))
1323: 	local win = vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()
1324: 	local buf = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
1325: 	vim.api.nvim_win_set_buf(win, buf)
1326: 	vim.api.nvim_set_current_win(win)
1327: 
1328: 	set_opt("filetype", "log", { buf = buf })
1329: 	set_opt("scrollback", 1000, { buf = buf })
1330: 
1331: 	C.state.job_id = vim.fn.termopen({ "curl", "-s", "-N", url }, {
1332: 		on_exit = function(_, exit_code, _)
1333: 			vim.schedule(function()
1334: 				if exit_code ~= 0 and C.state.win and is_win(C.state.win) then
1335: 					notify("Console connection lost", "warn")
1336: 				end
1337: 				C.state.job_id = nil
1338: 			end)
1339: 		end,
1340: 	})
1341: 
1342: 	C.state.win = win
1343: 	C.state.buf = buf
1344: 
1345: 	set_opt("wrap", true, { scope = "local", win = win })
1346: 	set_opt("number", false, { scope = "local", win = win })
1347: 	set_opt("relativenumber", false, { scope = "local", win = win })
1348: 	set_opt("signcolumn", "no", { scope = "local", win = win })
1349: 
1350: 	local km = vim.keymap.set
1351: 	km("n", "q", C.close, { buffer = buf, desc = "Hide console" })
1352: 	km("n", "c", C._terminal_clear, { buffer = buf, desc = "Clear console" })
1353: 	km("n", "<C-c>", C.close, { buffer = buf, desc = "Hide console" })
1354: 	disable_term_mode(buf)
1355: 	C._terminal_auto_clear()

1358: C._terminal_reconnect = function()
1359: 	local t = C.state.terminal
1360: 	if not C.state.buf then
1361: 		return
1362: 	end
1363: 	if t.attempts >= t.max_attempts then
1364: 		notify("Console reconnection failed: max attempts reached", "warn")
1365: 		return
1366: 	end
1367: 	local delay = t.delay * (2 ^ t.attempts)
1368: 	t.attempts = t.attempts + 1
1369: 	vim.defer_fn(function()
1370: 		if C.state.win and is_win(C.state.win) and C.state.mode == "terminal" then
1371: 			notify(string.format("Reconnecting to console (attempt %d)...", t.attempts), "info")
1372: 			C._open_terminal()
1373: 		end
1374: 	end, delay)
1375: end

1377: C._terminal_auto_clear = function()
1378: 	local t = C.state.terminal
1379: 	if t.timer then
1380: 		t.timer:close()
1381: 	end
1382: 	t.timer = vim.uv.new_timer()
1383: 	if t.timer then
1384: 		t.timer:start(t.clear_interval, t.clear_interval, function()
1385: 			vim.schedule(function()
1386: 				if not C.state.buf or not is_buf(C.state.buf) or C.state.mode ~= "terminal" then
1387: 					return
1388: 				end
1389: 				local now = os.time()
1390: 				if now - t.last_error > 30 then
1391: 					local lc = vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(C.state.buf)
1392: 					if lc > 100 then
1393: 						pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines, C.state.buf, 0, lc - 50, false, {})
1394: 					end
1395: 				end
1396: 			end)
1397: 		end)
1398: 	end

local function launch_browser()
	local chrome_cmd = core.find_chrome()
	if not chrome_cmd then
		notify("CDP: no Chrome/Chromium found in PATH", "warn")
		return
	end
	local server = require("p5.server")
	local url = server.port and string.format("http://localhost:%d", server.port) or nil
	local temp_dir = vim.fn.tempname()
	vim.fn.mkdir(temp_dir, "p")
	C.state.chrome_temp_dir = temp_dir
	local args = {
		chrome_cmd,
		"--remote-debugging-port=" .. C.config.remote_debugging_port,
		"--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1",
		"--user-data-dir=" .. temp_dir,
		"--no-first-run",
		"--no-default-browser-check",
	}
	local flags = C.config.browser_flags or {}
	for _, flag in ipairs(flags) do
		table.insert(args, flag)
	end
	if url then
		table.insert(args, url)
	end
	vim.fn.jobstart(args, { detach = true })
	notify("CDP: launched " .. chrome_cmd .. " with remote debugging on port " .. C.config.remote_debugging_port, "info")
end

local function close_browser()
	local temp_dir = C.state.chrome_temp_dir
	C.state.chrome_temp_dir = nil
	if C.config.close_browser_on_close and temp_dir then
		vim.fn.system({ "pkill", "-f", "--", temp_dir })
		vim.fn.delete(temp_dir, "rf")
	end
end

C._highlight_paused = function(url, line)
	C._clear_debug_highlights()
	if not url or not line then
		return
	end
	local project_root = vim.fn.getcwd()
	local path = url:match("^%a+://[^/]+(/.*)$") or url
	if path == url then
		path = "/" .. vim.fn.fnamemodify(url, ":t")
	end
	path = path:gsub("/$", "")
	local abs_path = project_root .. path
	local basename = vim.fn.fnamemodify(url, ":t")
	for _, buf in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_bufs()) do
		local name = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(buf)
		if name == abs_path or vim.fn.fnamemodify(name, ":t") == basename then
			pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark, buf, ns.debug, line - 1, 0, {
				sign_text = "●",
				sign_hl_group = "P5CDPDebugSign",
				hl_group = "P5CDPDebugCurrentLine",
				priority = 200,
			})
			local ok, win = pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_var, buf, "p5_sketch_win")
			if ok and win and is_win(win) then
				pcall(vim.api.nvim_set_current_win, win)
			end
			pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor, 0, { line, 0 })
			pcall(vim.cmd, "normal! zz")
			return
		end
	end
end
